verdict.headline: Walmart misses comps and cuts Q3 guidance, completing a 2-1 retail scorecard; BTC surges to $72K
verdict.label: WMT U.S. comps +2.6% vs. ~3.6% expected; Q3 EPS guide $0.62-$0.64 vs. $0.73 consensus; BABA +10% on AI cloud +45%; BTC ~$72,000 on $2.7B short squeeze; SPCX 319M-share tranche today; 0-of-3 regime indicators active
verdict.rationale_short: Walmart's Q2 FY27 report missed on comparable-store sales (2.6% vs. ~3.6% expected, with an 80bps health-and-wellness headwind) and delivered Q3 EPS guidance at $0.62-$0.64 against $0.73 consensus — sending WMT -8% pre-market and completing a two-and-one retail scorecard after HD (+1.7% comps, Aug 18) and TGT (+3.8% comps, Aug 19) both beat. FY27 net sales guidance was raised to +4-5%, confirming volume is intact; the deterioration is margin, not spending, which argues for a tariff-absorption read over broad demand deceleration. Against that, Alibaba reported AI cloud revenue +45% and triple-digit AI product revenue growth for the twelfth consecutive quarter — a constructive read-through for NVDA's August 26 print. Bitcoin surged to ~$72,000 on Bessent Treasury buyback liquidity and $2.7B in short liquidations. Level that changes the consumer read: WMT closes above its pre-print level by end of session, or management's 8 AM call explicitly attributes Q3 guide deterioration to tariff cost timing rather than demand softening.

trade_setups.asset: WMT — earnings call framing (8 AM ET today)
trade_setups.thesis: WMT's 2.6% comps miss and Q3 EPS guide at $0.62-$0.64 (vs. $0.73 consensus) completes a two-and-one retail scorecard. The critical distinction — tariff cost absorption or demand deceleration — resolves on the 8 AM call. FY27 net sales guidance raised to +4-5% confirms volume; the Q3 margin guide deterioration is the risk. Sector spillover question: whether consumer staples names (COST, KR) and consumer discretionary (AMZN) trade sympathetically to WMT's print, or whether the market reads it as WMT-specific.
trade_setups.entry: WMT pre-print close ~$115. Watch how retail sector spreads versus SPX through the session — WMT-specific means the spread compresses; structural means it widens. Consumer staples ETF (XLP) relative to SPX is the cleanest read-through instrument.
trade_setups.invalidation: Management attributes Q3 EPS guide to tariff cost timing with specific Q4 pass-through language, and WMT closes above $115 on the session.
trade_setups.horizon: Today's close through Q3 earnings season framing.

trade_setups.thesis: The August 20 tranche releases 319M shares — far exceeding the ~65M previously modeled — at a stock price of $136-145, above the $135 IPO price and $128 absorption floor. The Aug 6 first tranche (~20%) was absorbed at $105-115; the current range implies 20%+ appreciation since that event. The question is whether institutional demand at $135+ can absorb a supply event nearly five times larger than the prior model. WMT consumer stress and Brent approaching $94 are the competing macro headwinds on the same session.
trade_setups.entry: $128 absorption floor. Intraday range $136.72-$145.01. Close below $120 on elevated volume signals front-running of the tranche supply. Hold above $135 through close extends the absorption thesis into the late September next tranche.
trade_setups.invalidation: WMT -8% drives broader consumer/risk delevering, removing the marginal bid at $135+ and pushing SPCX below $120 on elevated volume before the close.
trade_setups.horizon: Today's session; next tranche late September.

trade_setups.asset: NVDA — six days to August 26 Q2 FY27 print
trade_setups.thesis: NVDA enters the final week before its Q2 FY27 earnings at $221.83 pre-market (+0.95%), with BABA's AI cloud +45% (12th consecutive quarter of triple-digit AI product growth) providing the most constructive demand read-through of the week. The setup has improved versus last week: 30Y is at 5.20% vs. 5.34% peak; AMD is recovering; BTC surge signals risk appetite intact. The bar remains: gross margin above 78% AND data-center guide materially above the most aggressive sell-side estimate — both simultaneously. Jackson Hole begins August 27, the morning after the print, eliminating any post-earnings de-risk window.
trade_setups.entry: Watch AMD's $484 containment signal (currently at $481) over the four pre-earnings sessions (Aug 20-25). AMD closing above $484 with volume is the clearest leading indicator that chip sector sentiment has reset from the Netlist DDR5 selloff. NVDA structural support $216; resistance $225.
trade_setups.invalidation: AMD closes below $450 before August 26, or WMT's guidance cut triggers a broad high-multiple risk-off delevering that resets SPX below 7,650.
trade_setups.horizon: August 26 after close; Jackson Hole August 27 opens immediately after.

bear_case: WMT's 2.6% comps miss and Q3 EPS guidance 15% below consensus arrives as the most comprehensive consumer data point of the retail gauntlet — 140 million weekly U.S. shoppers, all income cohorts, grocery and general merchandise. If the Q3 guide reflects tariff-driven cost absorption that WMT is not passing through, the pattern propagates across any retailer with comparable import exposure: 70% of WMT's products are sourced internationally. Brent at $92-93 is within one 1% session of breaching the $94 formal regime trigger, which would make two active indicators alongside the 30Y (5.20%). The BTC surge to $72,000 and BABA's +10% pre-market are short-squeeze and AI-cloud reads, respectively — neither directly addresses whether U.S. consumer margin compression is cyclical or structural. If WMT's earnings call frames Q3 guidance around demand softening rather than cost timing, the two-and-one retail scorecard becomes the first three-name consumer dataset that supports structural deceleration. Level that invalidates the equity resilience read: SPX closes below 7,650 within two sessions of today's open.
